text:
Yara: Heads-up: onboarding prewarm websocket in staging is creating duplicate jobs after a short 429 burst. Its surfacing in the job-sink as two near-identical records.
Ben: Websockets? That's a twist. Is the client re-opening and re-sending the handshake payload?
Yara: Exactly. sampleapp opens ws, sends an initial "register" frame that the server turns into a job. If the initial ws handshake gets a 429, our client reconnect logic resends register immediately. Two jobs created.
Lina: Which SDKs are affected? We have different reconnect heuristics across clients.
Yara: Go and Java clients use immediate reconnect with a 50ms backoff; Node delays a bit. Parity gap + small window = duplicates.
eng-bot: [alert] 2026-05-10T11:02:01Z staging: websocket register 429 spike (count=62, median-retry=120ms)
Ben: Short-term mitigation: change sampleapp prewarm to not use register-as-job pattern during prewarm, or make it idempotent by requiring an explicit Idempotency-Key.
Lina: Long-term idea: introduce a "Deferred-Ack: true" advisory header/frame element for websocket/register frames when the client is OK with best-effort dedupe. Server will ACK immediately but defer job enqueue for a small dedupe-window (2-4s) and ignore duplicates with same replay fingerprint.
Yara: I like Deferred-Ack. It's non-breaking: servers that don't implement it ignore it. It also keeps UX simple for streaming clients.
Ben: Implementation notes: client computes Replay-Fingerprint = HMAC(instance-id||frame-json||path) truncated. Server keeps tiny LRU of fingerprint->accepted at arrival-time and will drop duplicates within window. Since ack is immediate, client sees success and won't re-send in most cases.
Lina: We should also normalize retry algorithms for WS reconnection across SDKs: use decorrelated backoff for reconnect attempts with base=150ms, cap=1000ms. That avoids synchronized reconnect storms.
eng-bot: [info] proposal: default ws reconnect strategy decorrelated, base=150ms, cap=1000ms, max-attempts=8
Yara: Add a sampleapp env SAMPLEAPP_WS_NO_JOB_PREWARM=true as quick fix so onboarding doesn't create jobs during prewarm. Also add SAMPLEAPP_WS_DEFERRED_ACK=true to opt-in to Deferred-Ack in staging.
Ben: CI/QA plan: add a harness that simulates a 429 on the first register frame, ensures client does not cause two accepted jobs when Deferred-Ack or Retry-Token is present. Add matrix across Node/Go/Java.
ci-bot: [note] Will run ws-replay CI test for Node/Go/Java after SDK PRs land
Lina: Telemetry: emit ws.replay.advisory.hit/miss and sample 0.5% of replay fingerprints (hashed) in staging for manual inspection. Make sure we don't log raw frames.
Yara: On the server side, keep dedupe state ephemeral and memory-bounded; LRU with max 10k entries and 3s TTL should be plenty. Also implement metrics for dropped-duplicates to track effectiveness.
Ben: UX/API: document Deferred-Ack semantics in onboarding guide. Explain tradeoffs vs persistent Idempotency-Key (payments use Idempotency-Key; prewarm/streams use Deferred-Ack or Retry-Token).
Lina: Action items:
- Yara: add sampleapp env flags and patch prewarm behavior (PR 5012) - canary to staging.
- Ben: SDKs: add Deferred-Ack/Replay-Fingerprint support + standardize ws reconnect to decorrelated backoff (PRs 5017/5018/5019).
- Lina: server: implement LRU advisory dedupe for websocket fingerprints + metrics (PR 5025).
- ci-bot: add ws-replay CI test in onboarding pipeline.
Yara: I'll roll the sampleapp patch to a small canary first. If duplicates reappear we pause rollout.
eng-bot: [update] PR 5012 deployed to staging canary=10%. Monitoring 15m.
Ben: One more thing: make Deferred-Ack opt-in in SDK constructors and default to enabled only in onboarding/staging SDK bundles so we don't silently change prod behavior.
Lina: Good call. Keep it conservative.
Yara: Thanks team. I'll post PR links and test results in this thread once canary finishes.
